name: Karina Hamilton
life: “I still remember carrying my first rooted cutting in a paper straw.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Karina by a small Wednesday habit. Karina checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I took the original cutting on the day my husband came home. I want to root another for his brother.
appearance: Karina has dark brown curls cut close behind the ears, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a charcoal zip cardigan. It usually goes with a pen clipped inside the neckline. When somebody else has the floor, Karina squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Karina has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To root a cutting for the husband's brother.
family: Lina Farrell is Karina’s half-sibling. Karina picks the meeting place. Lina sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A room for a father*, Lina says, “I am the second wife's cousin. I can tell these people about a good father they never got.”
connections: Elsa Guzman. A rooted cutting is small enough to visit a patient who lacks ordinary callers.
